# Resolved fallback defaults — all constants

<!-- Regenerate: uv run python docs/schema/generate_skills.py -->

Applied when a field is unset at every tier (spec -> job-config.json).
Values are scraped from `resolution.py` / `schema.py` / `layout.py`
source, so this table is always current.

| Constant | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `DEFAULT_ARC_PRESERVE_COMPRESSION` | `True` | True = the non-uniform PLT glyph transforms (horizontal compression, the cap-line clamp, the descender relief, the italic shear) keep native AA arcs: each arc's ellipse image is refit with a short chain of circular arcs (bounded deviation, plt_optimizer/generate/arc_fit.py), so a compressed line emits ~1.05 arcs per source arc instead of ~2.8 polygonized line segments and engraves faster. False restores the historical polygonized output. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_AUTO_DESCENDING_CHARACTER_ADJUSTMENT` | `True` | `True` = a descending glyph is vertically downscaled and raised when a glyph on the FOLLOWING line comes within the required clearance (the engraved-stroke floor `0.5*(cutter_upper+cutter_lower)` scaled by 1 + `descending_character_clearance`) of it. The relief is per triggering glyph (never a blanket adjustment) and runs at render time; when the allowances are exhausted the gap below the line grows, and a collision that neither the allowances nor the admissible spacing can clear aborts the job. False = descenders engrave exactly as rendered. Cascades label/job (accepted on plates for schema parity only, never text lines); job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_BOLD_BOLDNESS_MULTIPLIER` | `1.5` | 1.5 = the multiplier inline `<b>` markup applies to target_boldness_factor on a multi-stroke (bold) PLT font (the bold runs re-run the cutter ladder at factor * multiplier, clamped to 0.30 with a WARNING). On single-stroke PLT and TTF fonts `<b>` instead steps to the next larger inventory cutter and this multiplier is inert. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_BOUNDARY_HOLE_CUTTER` | `0.015` | Boundary/hole cutter diameter feeding the collision stroke floor; `tools.json` `boundary_hole_cutter_size` overrides it. |
| `DEFAULT_BULLET_STRING` | `'•'` | Bullet-list marker used when `bullet_string` is unset at every tier. The derived bullet glyph (`fonts/glyph_transforms.py`), engraved by every PLT catalog font except the symbol fonts. Cascades item -> list block -> label -> job -> `job-config.json`; an explicit empty string engraves no marker. |
| `DEFAULT_COUNTER_PREFIX` | `''` | String prepended to each enumerate counter when `counter_prefix` is unset at every tier (empty = no prefix). |
| `DEFAULT_COUNTER_START_INDEX` | `1` | First counter value of an enumerate list when `counter_start_index` is unset at every tier. |
| `DEFAULT_COUNTER_STYLE` | `'decimal'` | Counter style of an enumerate list when `counter_style` is unset at every tier (the `decimal` value of `schema.CounterStyle`). One of `decimal`, `lower_alpha`, `upper_alpha`, `lower_roman`, `upper_roman`. |
| `DEFAULT_COUNTER_SUFFIX` | `''` | String appended to each enumerate counter when `counter_suffix` is unset at every tier (empty = no suffix). |
| `DEFAULT_CUTTER_DOWNSIZE` | `True` | `True` = the automatic cutter may be reduced one rung per allowed step when a text line is horizontally compressed past the midpoint between the current cutter and the next smaller inventory cutter (requires `tools.json` inventory; an explicit `cutter_size` disables it). |
| `DEFAULT_CUTTER_DOWNSIZE_GLOBAL` | `True` | `True` = a compression-driven cutter downsize is shared across the label: every other eligible line of the same `text_height` in the same label receives the trigger's final cutter (then each continues its own one-way loop; the group converges to the smallest). Explicit `cutter_size` / `cutter_downsize` false / `max_cutter_downsizes` 0 / `max_h_compress` 0.0 lines are never touched. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_CUTTER_DOWNSIZE_GLOBAL_JOB_WIDE` | `False` | `False` = the shared cutter downsize stays per-label. True = the sharing group widens from the label to the whole job: every eligible line of the same `text_height` in ANY label receives the trigger's final cutter, so one text size engraves with one tool job-wide. Requires `cutter_downsize_global` `true`; a line with this flag false keeps exactly the per-label behavior. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_CUTTER_LADDER_TOLERANCE` | `3.0` | 3.0 = the narrower/wider snap tolerance the ladder applies when a `<scale:N>` run's effective height `(N * text_height)` has no exact `tools.json` rung: it prefers the narrower tool unless that is more than tolerance x the distance to the wider tool away. The same tolerance the automatic line cutter uses; stored on the resolved line (with the inventory) as a ladder *input* so the per-run cutters re-derive identically in every pre-pass. Not a cascading schema field - the `<scale:N>` value rides the tag argument. |
| `DEFAULT_CUTTER_SIZE` | `None` | None = the text cutter is auto-selected from text_height (IDEAL_CUTTER_MAP + inventory snapping). An explicit cutter_size (line/label/job, no job-config tier) overrides the lookup: it snaps to the inventory (next size down, else up) and the toolpath height becomes `text_height - cutter_size`. |
| `DEFAULT_DESCENDING_CHARACTER_CLEARANCE` | `0.0` | 0.0 = the relief triggers only when the two engraved strokes would touch (the stroke floor); a unitless factor of that floor, so 0.3 demands 30% extra air and the requirement scales with the cutter width (reads the same at every text size). Cascades label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_DESCENDING_CHARACTER_RAISE` | `0.7` | 0.7 = a triggering descending glyph may be lifted by up to 70% of its own descender depth (1.0 lifts until its lowest point sits exactly at the baseline, 0.0 forbids raising). Cascades label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_DESCENDING_CHARACTER_RECIPROCAL_SCALE` | `0.5` | Deepest top-down downscale permitted for the would-be-colliding glyphs on the FOLLOWING line (`1.0` = reciprocal downscaling forbidden, the historical behavior; `0.5` = squeezed to half height). The lower glyphs are scaled about their own lowest ink point, so their lowest point never moves; they share the relief with the descending glyph through the same ramp driving its downscale/raise. Bound to `[0.2, 1.0]` by the schema. |
| `DEFAULT_DESCENDING_CHARACTER_V_SCALE` | `0.5` | 0.5 = a triggering descending glyph may be vertically squeezed to 50% of its height about its own baseline (1.0 forbids downscaling, 0.2 is the deepest squeeze). Cascades label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_ENFORCE_CAP_LINE` | `True` | `True` = every ASCII alphanumeric [0-9a-zA-Z] glyph whose ink extends above the per-font capline is downscaled top-down (a vertical scale about the glyph's own bottom, X untouched - the aspect ratio changes) so its top lands exactly on the capline. Strictly pre-markup: applied before the small-caps, bold, scale, italic and superscript/subscript transforms. Non-alphanumerics (punctuation, derived Unicode symbols) are never clamped. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_FALLBACK_ADVANCE_FRACTION` | `1.0` | Multiplier on the bounding-box-width fallback advance (no y-overlap or missing envelopes). 1.0 = the left glyph's own width. |
| `DEFAULT_FONT` | `'ReliefSingleLineCAD-Regular'` | Font fallback when unset at line/label/job level (and when job-config font is unset). Must be a valid font_registry name: a PLT-extracted catalog `font_name` key (arc-native) or a fonts/ TTF basename; run `generate_schema_docs.py --show-fonts`. |
| `DEFAULT_FONT_NAME` | `'ReliefSingleLineCAD-Regular'` | Registry-level default font name (font_registry.DEFAULT_FONT_NAME); resolution.DEFAULT_FONT mirrors it. |
| `DEFAULT_HOLE_ADJUST_FOR_CUTTER` | `True` | `True` = the emitted drill-hole circle shrinks by the boundary/hole cutter diameter (the cutter radius on each side of the hole's path) so the engraved hole measures the specified diameter: a 0.1in hole cut by a 0.015in cutter emits a 0.085in circle. The hole centre is placed from the specified diameter and never moves; a hole at or below the cutter diameter clamps to the smallest emittable circle (one plotter unit radius) with a WARNING. Cascades label/job (accepted on plates for schema parity only, never text lines); job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_HOLE_DIAMETER` | `0.125` | Drill-hole diameter when a hole entry omits 'diameter' (a job-config hole_diameter fills hole entries too). |
| `DEFAULT_HOLE_MARGIN` | `0.1875` | Hole margin when unset everywhere. Required from config-or-spec when a job-config is in play. |
| `DEFAULT_HOLE_TEXT_COLLISION_DISTANCE` | `0.15` | Engraved-stroke air gap on top of the stroke floor `0.5 * (hole_cutter + text_cutter)`. Required from config-or-spec when a job-config is in play (the shop `job-config.json` currently sets 0.1). |
| `DEFAULT_HTML_BRACKETS` | `'<>'` | Delimiter pair for the inline markup syntax (`<i>` italic and future tags): an even-length string whose first half is the left delimiter and second half the right (`"<>"` -> `<` / `>`). Text that legitimately contains chevrons opts out by declaring a pair absent from its data; a bracketed body that is not a registered tag engraves verbatim. The forward slash is only special inside the delimiters (`</i>`), never elsewhere. See `plt_optimizer.generate.markup`. |
| `DEFAULT_H_COMPRESS_GLOBAL` | `False` | `False` = horizontal compression stays per-line. `True` = a compressed line's scale is shared across the label: every other eligible line of the same `text_height` in the same label is compressed to the group's most-compressed (minimum) scale, clamped to each line's own 1 - `max_h_compress` budget floor. `max_h_compress` 0.0 lines are never touched. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_H_COMPRESS_GLOBAL_SAME_HEIGHT_ONLY` | `True` | `True` = the shared compression is scoped to the lines of the same `text_height` (one text size, one glyph density). `False` = the compression is shared across EVERY eligible line of the label, whatever its `text_height`, so one label engraves at one glyph density throughout. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_H_MARGIN` | `None` | Horizontal margin fall back to margin, then the default. Both are None to indicate "unset"; resolution logic fills them in. |
| `DEFAULT_ITALIC_ANGLE` | `12.0` | Slant angle (degrees) for italic markup: PLT-extracted glyphs (and TTF glyphs with no native italic face) are sheared about the baseline, $x' = x + y * tan(angle)$, so the baseline stays fixed and the glyph leans right. Bound to [0, 45] by the schema; 0 = upright (shear skipped). |
| `DEFAULT_KERNING_MIN_GAP_FRACTION` | `0.0` | Extra air added to every kerned pair advance on top of the cutter + character-spacing clearance, as a fraction of the rendered cap height (capline - baseline). 0.0 = no extra gap. |
| `DEFAULT_KERNING_PENETRATION_SCALE` | `1.0` | Multiplier on the detected windowed penetration (PLT-extracted fonts). 1.0 keeps the geometric penetration; >1.0 over-kerns tight pairs. |
| `DEFAULT_KERNING_RECESSION_SCALE` | `1.0` | Multiplier on a *recessed* (negative) detected penetration (PLT-extracted fonts). 1.0 keeps the geometric recession (the historical linear behavior); 0.0 makes a recessed pair advance by nothing beyond the min_glyph_width_fraction floor, so the penetration dial only tightens pairs whose silhouettes overlap. |
| `DEFAULT_KERNING_WINDOW_FRACTION` | `0.05` | Kerning window (fraction of the rendered text height, in [0.0, 1.0]). For PLT-extracted fonts. Each envelope sample compares against the opposite silhouette within +/- (half of this fraction) of the text height and the effective penetration is the worst windowed penetration, so staggered pokes widen the advance; 0.0 reproduces the historical same-height maximum-penetration kerning. |
| `DEFAULT_KERN_NEG_STRING` | `None` | `None` = the manual-kern negative marker is disabled. When set (`kern_neg_string`), every occurrence is stripped and the following character's cursor retreats by `kern_width_fraction` of the cap height (no clamp, so a large value lets glyphs overlap). Same validation as `kern_pos_string`; the two strings must differ. |
| `DEFAULT_KERN_POS_STRING` | `None` | `None` = the manual-kern positive marker is disabled (no occurrence is stripped). When set (`kern_pos_string`, cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default), every occurrence of the string in a text line is stripped - it never engraves - and the following character's cursor advances by `kern_width_fraction` of the cap height. Multi-character markers are legal ('<->'); the value must be non-empty, newline-free, and not markup-shaped (a letters-only body like `<s>` is consumed by the tag scan, so the schema rejects it; the resolution-time check validates against the effective `html_brackets`). Works on PLT and TTF fonts. |
| `DEFAULT_KERN_WIDTH_FRACTION` | `0.1` | 0.1 = the manual-kern width as a fraction of the rendered cap height (capline - baseline): one marker shifts the cursor by this fraction of the cap height (positive string forward, negative backward; adjacent markers accumulate). Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. Explicit 0.0 is honored (markers consume their characters, shift nothing). |
| `DEFAULT_LABEL_SHAPE` | `'rect'` | Fallback label boundary shape when the `type` cascade resolves to unset. See :attr:`plt_optimizer.generate.schema.LabelAttributes.type`. |
| `DEFAULT_LINE_SPACING` | `'auto'` | Extra line spacing when unset at line/label/job level. |
| `DEFAULT_LIST_MARKER_GAP_FRACTION` | `0.5` | Gap between a list marker and its text, as a fraction of the line's rendered cap height, when `list_marker_gap_fraction` is unset at every tier. The marker column is the widest marker of the list plus this gap. |
| `DEFAULT_MARGIN` | `0.125` | Label margin when unset at label/job level. |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_CUTTER_DOWNSIZES` | `1` | Maximum number of cutter downsizings per text line (0 = disabled). Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_MAX_H_COMPRESS` | `0.0` | 0.0 = horizontal compression disabled. Required from config-or-spec when a job-config is in play. |
| `DEFAULT_MIN_GLYPH_WIDTH_FRACTION` | `0.0` | Global minimum glyph advance width (as a fraction of the rendered cap height, capline - baseline) for PLT-extracted fonts. The profile-envelope kerning floors each pair's advance at this fraction of the cap height, capped by the left glyph's own width; 0.0 means pure envelope kerning. |
| `DEFAULT_MIN_HOLE_MARGIN` | `None` | None = collision avoidance may shrink hole_margin all the way to 0.0. Required from config-or-spec when a job-config is in play. |
| `DEFAULT_MULTISTROKE_OVERLAP_RATIO` | `0.25` | 0.25 = the minimum overlap fraction between adjacent cutter passes of a multi-stroke (bold) PLT font: the derived cutter is never smaller than `pass_spacing / (1 - ratio)`, so engraved passes always overlap and no unengraved stripe appears. The actual overlap is derived from the chosen cutter and logged. Inert on single-stroke fonts, TTF fonts, and lines with an explicit `cutter_size`. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZE_LINE_CONTENT` | `False` | `False` = every text line keeps its authored words. `True` = consecutive enabled lines exchange whole words (word order kept, only the line breaks move) so the group's natural rendered widths equalize, minimizing the compression the label needs. A disabled line breaks the group; runs of one line, blank lines and groups with fewer words than lines are left alone. Runs as an export pre-pass before the cutter-reduction and shared-compression pre-passes. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_OPTIMIZE_LINE_CONTENT_MAX_LINES` | `None` | Ceiling on the consecutive lines one reflow group may use. `None` (the default) is *unset*: the group reflows across its existing lines and never gains one. The option is growth-only -- a numeric value may ADD lines to a label (the group starts at its existing line count and grows while its lines still need horizontal compression) and never removes any. Consumed by :mod:`plt_optimizer.generate.line_content`. |
| `DEFAULT_PLATE_HEIGHT` | `16.0` | Auto-allocated (unbounded mode) default plate height when job-config `plate_height` is unset. Required from config when a job-config is in play and plates are undeclared. |
| `DEFAULT_PLATE_WIDTH` | `24.0` | Auto-allocated (unbounded mode) default plate width when job-config `plate_width` is unset. Required from config when a job-config is in play and plates are undeclared. |
| `DEFAULT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE_FRACTION` | `0.0` | Fallback rectangular-border corner rounding fraction when the `rounded_rectangle_fraction` cascade resolves to unset (see :attr:`plt_optimizer.generate.schema.LabelAttributes.rounded_rectangle_fraction`). `0.0` is the sharp rectangle, bit-identical to the historical border. |
| `DEFAULT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE_PROPORTIONAL` | `False` | Fallback proportional-rounding flag when the `rounded_rectangle_proportional` cascade resolves to unset (see :attr:`plt_optimizer.generate.schema.LabelAttributes.rounded_rectangle_proportional`). `False` uses one identical rounding distance on every side (the shorter edge determines it). |
| `DEFAULT_SC_SCALE` | `0.7` | 0.7 = a small-caps font (a font name ending in ' SC', a synthetic variant of the base font) renders ASCII lowercase a-z as the base font's uppercase glyph uniformly shrunk to 70% of the cap height, top-down (the glyph's own bottom stays in place, its top descends). Uppercase and caseless characters engrave at full size and the nominal text_height is untouched (no cutter change). 1.0 renders the variant identically to its base font; the field is inert on a non-SC font. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_SPACE_WIDTH_FRACTION` | `0.3` | Space advance (PLT-extracted fonts) as a fraction of the rendered text height: a space advances `DEFAULT_SPACE_WIDTH_FRACTION * text_height + character_spacing`. |
| `DEFAULT_STRIKETHROUGH_BREAK_SPACES` | `False` | False = an inline `<s>` strikethrough draws one continuous stroke across the whole struck run, inter-word spaces included. True ends the stroke at each space, so every word gets its own strike spanning its own ink and the space stays bare. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_STRIKETHROUGH_OFFSET_FRACTION` | `None` | `None` = an inline `<s>` strikethrough centres its centerline stroke on the cap-band midline (half the rendered cap height), the classic mid-height strike. An explicit value is the stroke's height as a fraction of the rendered cap height (`capline - baseline`) ABOVE the baseline (0.0 = the stroke sits on the baseline, 1.0 = on the capline). The stroke spans each struck run's ink width and is cut with the run's own text cutter; unlike the underline it is NEVER broken, so a descender punches through it (no clearance, no break test). Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_SUPERSUBSCRIPT_DOWNSCALE` | `0.5` | 0.5 = a bare `<sup>`/`<sub>` markup run engraves its glyphs uniformly shrunk to 50% of the line's size, and the baseline shift derives from the same number, centering the shrunken glyph on the line it belongs to: a superscript rises $1 - d/2 = 0.75$ cap heights (its centre lands exactly on the capline) and a subscript drops $d/2 = 0.25$ cap heights (its centre lands on the baseline). The argumented forms `<sup:0.3>`/`<sub:-0.2>` set the shift explicitly in cap-height units (bound [-1.0, 1.0]) and apply no scaling, so this field is inert on them. A downscaled run engraves with the cutter for its downscaled height (the `<scale:N>` ladder), so it lands on its own per-cutter layer. Bound [0.2, 1.0]. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_TARGET_BOLDNESS_FACTOR` | `0.14` | 0.14 = the target engraved stroke width (as a fraction of text height) for multi-stroke (bold) PLT fonts (`stroke_count` > 1 in the font's catalog file). The automatic cutter is sized so the N engraved passes total this width, then snapped to the inventory (stepping up when the snap-down breaks the gap-free floor). Inert on single-stroke fonts, TTF fonts, and lines with an explicit cutter_size. Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_TEXT_COLOR` | `'none'` | Implicit stroke-color layer of text that omits text_color (never cascades; a job-level text_color is rejected). 'none' cannot be specified explicitly. |
| `DEFAULT_TEXT_HEIGHT` | `0.25` | Font height when unset at line/label/job level. |
| `DEFAULT_TEXT_H_ALIGNMENT` | `'center'` | Horizontal alignment fallback when unset everywhere. |
| `DEFAULT_UNDERLINE_BREAK_CLEARANCE_FRACTION` | `0.0` | Extra air at each underline break, as a fraction of the rendered cap height (capline - baseline). Each cut is padded horizontally by `0.5 * cutter + fraction * cap height` (the half cutter is the glyph stroke's own half-width -- the ink is a centerline), so the engraved air between a descending glyph's stroke and the underline's cut edge is exactly this clearance (0.0 = the cut sits at the ink). Independent of the offset (which decides which glyphs break); this adds air at the break itself. The code fallback is 0.0 (the historical cut); job-config.json supplies the shop default. See `plt_optimizer.generate.underline`. |
| `DEFAULT_UNDERLINE_BREAK_SPACES` | `False` | Whether an underline (`<u>`) breaks at the spaces between words. `False` (the default) draws one continuous underline across the whole underlined run (spaces included, broken only by descending glyphs); `True` ends the underline at each space, so every word gets its own underline spanning its own ink and the inter-word space stays bare. The code fallback is `False` (the historical continuous underline); job-config.json supplies the shop default. See `plt_optimizer.generate.label_renderer._underline_render_gate`. |
| `DEFAULT_UNDERLINE_OFFSET_FRACTION` | `0.0` | Extra air for underline markup (`<u>`) as a fraction of the rendered cap height (capline - baseline). The underline is a centerline stroke cut with the line's own text cutter, positioned `cutter diameter + fraction * cap height` below the baseline, so the engraved underline's top edge floats exactly `fraction * cap height` below the engraved baseline stroke. The break test is strictly horizontal: a glyph breaks the underline where its ink crosses the underline's centerline (dipping past `cutter diameter + fraction * cap height` below the baseline), so the offset alone decides which glyphs break. 0.0 = the underline's top edge touches the baseline stroke and gaps only where strokes truly cross. See `plt_optimizer.generate.underline`. |
| `DEFAULT_USE_BASELINE_SPACING` | `True` | `True` = a label's text lines stack by baseline pitch (cap height + `line_spacing`), so descenders hang into the gap below their line and every gap reads as one uniform visual spacing; auto `line_spacing` and the margin clamp measure each line's real descender extent. `False` = lines stack by rendered ink box (historical), where a descender inflates the gap under its own line. Cascades label/job (accepted on plates for schema parity only, never text lines); job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_V_CENTER_BY_CONTENT` | `False` | Vertical centering mode for a label's text block. `False` (the default) centers the block by its **baseline-to-capline band** -- the band spans the lowest baseline to the highest capline, so the visible text is optically centered and descenders hang into the bottom margin, where the descending- character relief handles them against the bottom border. `True` centers by the block's **rendered ink** (the historical behavior): the deepest descender is charged to the block, so a line carrying descenders rides high in the label. Band centering is active only when the descending-character relief is enabled (see `center_text_by_band`); with the relief off nothing would adjust the descenders, so ink centering is kept. Label-level only -- centering is a property of the stacked block, never of one line, so the field is deliberately absent from `TextLine`/`TextAttributes`. |
| `DEFAULT_V_CENTER_CHARS` | `''` | '' = the auto-apply is OFF by default (every pre-feature line renders bit-identically); job-config.json ships the shop set '-:–—=<>' = the characters auto-centred vertically between the baseline and the capline: every text character occurring in this string is raised or lowered (a pure vertical translate) so its own ink is centred on the cap-band midline (half the rendered cap height above the baseline) -- the characters a font typically draws too high (hyphen, colon, en/em dash, '=', '<', '>'). The inline `<vc>...</vc>` markup tag applies the same centering to any other characters it wraps. An empty string disables the auto-apply (the `<vc>` tag keeps working on its own). Cascades line/label/job; job-config supplies the shop default. |
| `DEFAULT_V_MARGIN` | `None` | Vertical margin fall back to margin, then the default. Both are None to indicate "unset"; resolution logic fills them in. |
